Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36966: bench: fix `InputType` ODR violation

66654bc5ce9b1cf9613346107b9520ad003a68c4 ci: add CMAKE_INTERPROCEDURAL_OPTIMIZATION to Alpine job (fanquake)
307b22b59d4417f1f99fe7af8e36b3285045ce8b bench: put InputType enums in anonymous namespaces (fanquake)

Pull request description:

  Introduced in #36475:
  ```bash
  /ci_container_base/src/bench/bip352.cpp:22:12: error: type ‘InputType’ violates the C++ One Definition Rule [-Werror=odr]
     22 | enum class InputType {
        |            ^
  /ci_container_base/src/bench/sign_transaction.cpp:24:12: note: an enum with different value name is defined in another translation unit
     24 | enum class InputType {
        |            ^
  /ci_container_base/src/bench/bip352.cpp:23:5: note: name ‘P2PKH’ differs from name ‘P2WPKH’ defined in another translation unit
     23 |     P2PKH,           // legacy pubkey-hash
        |     ^
  /ci_container_base/src/bench/sign_transaction.cpp:25:5: note: mismatching definition
     25 |     P2WPKH, // segwitv0, witness-pubkey-hash (ECDSA signature)
        |     ^
  ```

  There's a commit here that adds a CI config, using GCC and LTO, which uses `-Wodr`. The existing LTO config uses Clang, and I'm not sure about adding LTO to any existing job. However I do think we should be catching ODR violations in CI.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36830: test: make `tx_mempool_block_doublespend` cases independent

0d98c438ebc124ca4252bdd2855d62691e030e58 test: make tx_mempool_block_doublespend spends conflicting (Alexander Wiederin)
07540640aa49e357b78523efc4f6c13c3a51a5cc test: split tx_mempool_block_doublespend into independent test cases (Alexander Wiederin)

Pull request description:

  Found during #36692: remove test state that is shared and modified across cases.

  `tx_mempool_block_doublespend` ran four cases against one chain and mempool, removing each case’s mempool transaction by hand before the next one. Each case is now its own test with a fresh setup that builds the two spends. The first commit also fixes the last case’s comment, which had the mempool and block spends reversed. The checks are unchanged.

  The second commit makes the two spends distinct transactions. Previously they were identical (deterministic signing), so in the last case the mempool transaction was removed because it was mined rather than as a conflict. The rejection cases are unaffected: they fail with `bad-txns-inputs-missingorspent` either way.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36109: test: fix coinbases built on arbitrary parents

b7b762880e7583a06429f9eca525670a2ee18e5e test: pad fork coinbase input scripts (Lőrinc)
5cdbfd5f01a27e1068f05b21b12c8f269083a4dc test: derive fork subsidy from parent (Lőrinc)
33bbf91e1ae661e98017049d0315974a1f772255 test: derive fork difficulty from parent (Lőrinc)
4745be9837fbfef176e0cb226ab04289f33b0090 refactor: extract fork block reconstruction (Lőrinc)
bf551335bebe4ff4d8d62e378b4302eb782709e6 test: characterize fork coinbase fields (Lőrinc)

Pull request description:

  **Problem:** Test helpers that attach active-tip templates to arbitrary parents retain the template's subsidy.
  Existing reorg tests can pass with underpaid coinbases.
  A fork crossing a halving can overpay and fail with `bad-cb-amount`.
  At heights 1 through 16, encoding only the height leaves the coinbase input script too short and triggers `bad-cb-length`.

  **Fix:** Share parent-dependent reconstruction between `BuildChain()` and `MinerTestingSetup::Block()`, deriving difficulty and coinbase fields from the actual parent.
  Pad rebuilt coinbase input scripts.
  Require coinbase-only templates so replacing the reward with the subsidy cannot discard transaction fees.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36293: contrib: exclude inactive keys from the binary quorum by default

034271d4e1739347a31c64dbc4bfef8aa133ad1d doc: explain inactive binary signature handling (Lőrinc)
eff64984f5994347f8e28aa57e0394f80c87129b contrib: allow expired keys for old releases (Lőrinc)
02939e424d3834c1db94c3fbd8ce731ec6e28e41 contrib: exclude and report expired signatures (Lőrinc)
20e15a5fdc5dea8ffc18c91a0d088dba8de2215c contrib: exclude revoked keys from binary quorum (Lőrinc)
431cac72734c267e9722f31667a05c7ce8c6ae91 test: characterize inactive signature quorum (Lőrinc)

Pull request description:

  **Problem:** The binary verifier counts signatures from expired and revoked keys toward `--min-good-sigs`.
  Enough of these signatures can satisfy the threshold without any active signing key, and they are returned as good signatures.

  **Fix:** Warn about expired and revoked signatures and exclude them from threshold counting by default.
  For historical verification, expired signatures can count toward the threshold with `--allow-expired` or `BINVERIFY_ALLOW_EXPIRED`, including signatures created after key expiry. Revoked signatures remain excluded.
  Expired signatures are reported separately, including in the `expired_sigs` field in successful JSON output.

  The decision uses GnuPG’s current key status from the local keyring, even if the signature was created while the key was active.

  This was found and disclosed responsibly by the Red Team 🟥.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#34909: wallet, refactor: modularise wallet by extracting out legacy wallet migration

9fd8e543b3ceed08a4bb8ce3d8d342195403056e wallet, refactor: rename file from migrate to legacybdb (rkrux)
f726ef740fae2e73f112a48981fd08cda0ae9c09 wallet: extract out migration specific LegacySPKM CWallet methods (rkrux)
e8165d533191e42ab4f8dd52e9233e13ff8f1262 wallet: extract out public facing MigrateLegacyToDescriptor functions (rkrux)
156249d75e0f9342015dc114fe1cf2210325d094 wallet: extract out utility functions from wallet/wallet to wallet/walletutil.h (rkrux)
5c8b0872b62a35d33461bb6d4c9b306a562b1f63 wallet: (move-only) extract out migration specific CWallet methods (rkrux)

Pull request description:

  I've been meaning to scratch this itch for quite some time. It has been noted
  by many developers that the `wallet/wallet.cpp` file is quite hard to reason
  about.

  It is more than 4500 lines long currently and this patch is an attempt to
  shortern it by around 800 lines by extracting out the wallet migration code into
  a dedicated `wallet/migration.cpp` file.

  The other benefits of this PR I see are that it moves the legacy wallet stuff
  from the main wallet file that paves the way for it being descriptor specific
  (as much as possible), and makes legacy wallet migration code a first-class
  citizen in its own file.

  I hope it makes it easier for everyone to go through the main wallet file.

  This patchset **should** be reviewed with --color-moved=dimmed-zebra option.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36908: mining: avoid checkBlock crash when chain has no tip

8cba4bace8df92afcc9ff46404e36c741d557b64 mining: avoid checkBlock crash when chain has no tip (Turtlecute33)

Pull request description:

  **The problem**: `Init.makeMining` returns as soon as the chainstate is loaded. On a first start with an empty datadir, or on a node started with `-reindex`/`-reindex-chainstate`, this is before the genesis block is connected, so the active chain has no tip. A `Mining.checkBlock` call in this window reaches `TestBlockValidity()`, which asserts that the tip exists, and the node aborts.

  **The fix**: in `MakeMining`, if `wait_loaded` is set, wait for the chainstate to be present and for the tip to be non-null.

  *Alternative fix*: In `Mining.checkBlock`, check if the tip is present, return early with "inconclusive-no-chain-tip" otherwise. (I initially implemented this fix, but decided to go with the `makeMining` one instead, see https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36908#discussion_r4610682758)

  The crash can be reproduced on master using the functional test included in this PR.

  This is joint work with Turtlecute33 :)

  w0xlt:
    ACK 8cba4bace8df92afcc9ff46404e36c741d557b64
  xyzconstant:
    tACK 8cba4bace8
  ryanofsky:
    Code review ACK 8cba4bace8df92afcc9ff46404e36c741d557b64. This extends the #34661 fix to cover a case it missed. #34661 made `makeMining` wait for the chainstate to be loaded, but on a first start or with `-reindex`/`-reindex-chainstate` the chainstate is loaded before genesis is connected, and a `checkBlock` call in between still hits the `Tip()` assert in `TestBlockValidity`. `makeMining` now also waits for a tip using the same condition `AppInitMain` waits for before starting the node.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36863: test: fix wallet tests that check the wrong wallet

13b2d21bebb0d84847e1c42f96db280058e7b0a6 test: check w8, not w7, after creating the avoid_reuse wallet (w0xlt)
215f8b828bc5c85b6a662c1424902e25c23ec6c0 test: restore each node's own wallet backup in wallet_keypool_topup (w0xlt)

Pull request description:

  `wallet_keypool_topup.py` is meant to test keypool restore for four output types, one node each. But the wallet and backup paths are only set for node1, so for nodes 2-4 the test copies node1's backup over node1's running wallet and restarts the node under test on its own, never-restored wallet. The checks still pass, so only the legacy case has actually been tested since 0dcac51049.

  This backs up and restores each node's own wallet, and asserts that the restored wallet rescans on startup so the test can't silently skip the restore again. Adding just that assertion on master makes the test fail at node2.

  Also fixes `wallet_createwallet.py` calling `w7.walletpassphrase` where it means w8 (since c5d3787367), so the `avoid_reuse wallet` was never checked.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#35756: cmake: De-duplicate libraries where possible

e6c1483832e018ccafc04fdc4faf051d13fc09d4 guix: Turn macOS linker warnings into errors (Hennadii Stepanov)
1714370aa60ce88941ae95b06f4eb6d7dae1650a cmake: De-duplicate libraries where possible (Hennadii Stepanov)

Pull request description:

  Set the [CMP0156](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/policy/CMP0156.html) and [CMP0179](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/policy/CMP0179.html) policies to NEW. CMP0156 de-duplicates libraries on link lines based on linker capabilities; CMP0179 makes this de-duplication keep the first occurrence of static libraries. This silences Apple linker "ignoring duplicate libraries" warnings.

  Both policies are gated on CMP0179, which requires CMake >=3.31, to avoid the intermediate CMake 3.29/3.30 behaviour where only CMP0156 is available. This requirement is satisfied by the current Homebrew package and the Guix build environment. On older versions, the policy guard makes this a no-op.

  The Guix scripts for macOS have been updated to turn linker warnings into errors, as is [done](https://github.com/fanquake/bitcoin/commit/1714953eff0544d6085c4c1cc4270a891dd995c0) for other targets.

commit.message:
wallet, refactor: rename file from migrate to legacybdb

The wallet/migrate.h|cpp file contain all the code related to the
Berkeley DB that was used in the legacy wallets. Although it's true
that this code is used only within the context of wallet migration
but the name of the file is not exact.

This patch renames the file to legacybdb so that the intent is clearer in the
call sites. I felt this rename might be necessary so that the name
doesn't conflict with the new migration.cpp introduced in the preceding commits.
